That condition will save energy and enhance the network lifetime whenever it is feasible. Gravity function plays a preeminent role in the selection of the relay node. In order to tackle the Congruent gravity value, the cluster head selection technique is used. Network Simulator has been used to evaluate the performance of CGV, and its results are compared with ER2PR, VBF, and UFCA. These protocols utilized a large area in order to select a relay node. To overcome this problem, CGV used just those area which is best for the selection of the relay node and response packet transmission area is also minimize whenever it is feasible by the condition.

Author Keywords: UWSN, Congruent Gravity, ER2PR, VBF, UFCA, Network Simulator NS-2

articleTitle: Server Based Task Allocation to Reduce Inter-Task Memory Interference in Multicore Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Frontiers of Information Technology (FIT)
abstract: In multicore systems tasks running on one core may experience inter-task interference from tasks running on other cores. This inter-task interference is due to contention in using shared resources such as caches, system bus and the main memory. In this work, we focus on one of the major sources of cross-core interference in multicore systems, i.e., main memory. The idea is to allocate tasks to cores in a way that the total memory demand of all tasks executing at a time instant t is less than the minimum available memory bandwidth, i.e., DRAM min. The problem is formulated as a server-to-core mapping problem where each server constitute a set of tasks corresponding to an application. As mapping problems in multicore systems are NP-hard, we use different heuristic and meta-heuristic based approaches to find a feasible solution. Results show that our approach can perform well in multicore systems with ≤ 8 processing cores with the memory demand of each server upper bounded by DRAM min/2.

articleTitle: Test Case Prioritization Based on Path Complexity
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Frontiers of Information Technology (FIT)
abstract: Software undergoes many modifications after its release. Regression testing is performed to ensure that the modification has not introduced any errors in the software and the software continues to work correctly. Regression testing is an expensive process. Three types of cost reduction techniques are used in regression testing. These techniques i.e., test case selection, test suite minimization and test case prioritization are used to reduce the cost of regression testing and improve the rate of fault detection. The focus of our research is on test case prioritization. Instead of minimizing test suite or selecting fewer test cases, test case prioritization orders test cases in such a way that the test cases detecting more faults are executed earlier. In case of limited resources, only top priority test cases are executed to ensure the reliability of the software. In this research, we have proposed an approach which uses path complexity and branch coverage to prioritize test cases based on assumption that the complex code is more likely to contain faults. Halstead's metric has been used to calculate the path complexity of the test cases. Proposed approach is compared with branch coverage based prioritization technique using some example programs. The results show that proposed approach outperforms existing branch coverage based approach in terms of APFD (Average Percentage of Faults Detected) up to 18% on average.

articleTitle: Heterogeneous 2-Phase Method for Strongly Connected Components Detection and Classification of Graphs
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Frontiers of Information Technology (FIT)
abstract: Different sequential and parallel methods exist for decomposing a directed graph into its Strongly Connected Components (SCCs). To speed up the execution for very large graphs, Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) have been used. The real-world graphs have small-world property with a single giant SCC and many small-sized SCCs. For such graphs, two-phase methods have been used with different parallelism strategies, both on CPU and GPU in the previous research. Our research indicates that the existing methods have great variance in their performances for different types of graphs. This research classifies the graphs on the basis of which method works best for them after analyzing their properties. Such classification ensures applying the best SCC detection method in case the type of the input graph is known. We have also developed a new method that has consistently better performance for all types of graphs. This method can be used when the type of the input graph is not known or it doesn't fit into the classification. In this method, the first phase is run on the GPU whereas the second phase is run on the CPU using either sequential or multithreaded routine.

articleTitle: Forensics Analysis of Wish-Shopping Made Fun Application on Android
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Frontiers of Information Technology (FIT)
abstract: Nowadays in the digital world, the Internet has become the desired medium to perform actions in daily lives. Shopping over the internet has made lives easier and comfortable. Internet users' attitudes towards online shopping are not entirely consistent. They wanted to utilize the plastic money to shop online simultaneously they feel themselves at risk to share their credit card information. As the popularity increases so do the trend to shop online increases. While using mobile devices there might be some residual data left behind in those devices. In the e-commerce domain, it is being difficult for the forensics analyst to identify sensitive information and observe the user's behavior. In this paper, we have identified and evaluate the forensically sound remnants left in a mobile device with an experimental analysis of wish application. The location containers found during the analysis will be useful for investigators to build case scenarios. With exhaustive research of wish architecture, we have summarized the artifacts in tabular form. It is composed of an artifact's location and identification type of those remnants.

Author Keywords: E commerce application forensics, Mobile forensics, Wish app, Online shopping, Android forensics

articleTitle: Security Against Compromised Servers: Verifiable DB Queries
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Frontiers of Information Technology (FIT)
abstract: In these days almost every application on the Internet relies on a type of database to store client data on the server side. These databases are often used to store session identifiers, financial details, medical records, and other privacy-critical data. Consequently, security of these databases is very critical, but it cannot be guaranteed due to modern software complexity and ease in launching cyber-attacks. So if some intruder gets access the database, then he can change the user data to negatively impact the interest and safety of data owner. In this paper, we have proposed a solution to this problem and demonstrated in form of a proof-of-concept. Our solution provides cryptographic proof with each database query. This helps end client to verify the result in real time with minimum overhead even in fully compromised server-side environment. A successful verification status means that the result of database query is correct, complete, and fresh. Our proposed solution consists of database query verification components including (i) query verification client, (ii) query verification server and (iii) blockchain. We have implemented the proof-of-concept in node.js, and evaluation results show that it can work in real time with minimal overhead while guaranteeing freshness, completeness and correctness of data.

articleTitle: Erlang Based Server Selection Scheme Using Software Defined Networking in Datacenter for Energy Conservation
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Frontiers of Information Technology (FIT)
abstract: Big Data, IoT and progression of Internet has resulted in exponential growth of datacenters. Datacenter optimizations are required to address the growth challenges with acceptable Quality of Services (QoS) at a reasonable cost. Datacenters are characterized by heterogeneous hardware platforms and a number of homogeneous servers to execute tasks having distinct characteristics such as time, origin, density and class of service. Large scale datacenters need efficient mechanisms to handle incoming requests by ensuring availability of optimal number of servers. Otherwise, it may result in poor QoS and/or unstable economy of operations due to idle or under-utilized servers. A suitable load distribution mechanism helps in minimizing unnecessary resource consumption, addressing failures, scalability, eliminating bottlenecks and overprovisioning etc. and hence enhances overall performance. There are various techniques such as non-proactive or reactive load balancing to address these challenges in datacenters. This paper implements an Erlang based approach to control server allocation in Software Defined Networking (SDN) based datacenters. The proposed approach handles the aforementioned challenges using proactive use of Erlang distribution of services along with centralized control plane architecture of SDN, thus maximizing energy efficiency, and ensuring optimal performance of services. The results present a comparison of proposed algorithm with some of the most common approaches.
